faqs.question: When is Ganpati Visarjan in 2026?
faqs.answer: The main ganpati visarjan 2026 is on Friday 25 September, the day of Anant Chaturdashi. Ganesh Chaturthi itself is Monday 14 September 2026, so the big immersion is the eleventh day, not the tenth.

faqs.question: What are the other visarjan dates in 2026 if I am not keeping Bappa for ten days?
faqs.answer: Five shorter observances immerse on 14 September (same day), 15 September (dedh din), 16 September (third day), 18 September (fifth day) and 20 September (seventh day). All the popular immersion days fall on odd counts from Chaturthi.

faqs.question: What time should the visarjan be done on 25 September 2026?
faqs.answer: For Mumbai, Drik Panchang gives an auspicious morning window of 6:28 AM to 10:59 AM and an afternoon Shubha window of 12:30 PM to 2:01 PM. Timings shift with local sunrise, so check the choghadiya for your own city.

faqs.question: Can I do Ganpati visarjan at home in a bucket?
faqs.answer: Yes, and CPCB's 2020 guidelines actively prefer it for small household idols. Keep the idol fully immersed until it dissolves, add alum, stir vigorously for 30 seconds and then slowly for 30 more, and let it settle.

faqs.question: What do I do with the water and mud after a home visarjan?
faqs.answer: CPCB says the clear water on top can go into the garden or a drain once the solids have settled. Dry the settled mud and reuse it for a plant pot or for next year's idol.

faqs.question: Are PoP Ganpati idols actually banned?
faqs.answer: CPCB's Revised Guidelines for Idol Immersion of 12 May 2020 say idols made of plaster of Paris 'shall be banned', along with thermocol, single-use plastic and oil paints. It is a guideline rather than a statute, and enforcement has varied by state and by year.

faqs.question: How do I tell a shadu clay idol from a PoP one in the shop?
faqs.answer: Weight is the giveaway. CPCB notes PoP became popular precisely because it is lighter and cheaper than clay, so a large idol you can lift easily with one hand is almost certainly not shadu maati.

faqs.question: Does immersing one small idol really change the water?
faqs.answer: One idol does not, but the season does. Mumbai alone recorded 1,97,114 immersions on the last day of Ganeshotsav 2025, and measured dissolved oxygen in three Nagpur lakes fell to 0.89-2.34 mg/L after the immersion season.

faqs.question: Is an artificial pond as good as a lake for visarjan?
faqs.answer: It is better for the water body, because the pollutants stay contained and the sludge is cleared instead of settling in a lake. Roughly 40% of Mumbai's 2025 immersions used the city's 290-plus artificial ponds.

faqs.question: What happens to all the nirmalya after visarjan?
faqs.answer: In Mumbai the civic body collects it separately for composting rather than letting it go into the water. Around 508 metric tonnes of flowers, leaves and garlands were collected during Ganeshotsav 2025.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganpati Visarjan 2026: Dates, Muhurat and the Water Question

Ganpati visarjan 2026 falls on **Friday 25 September**, Anant Chaturdashi, eleven days after Ganesh Chaturthi on **Monday 14 September**. Shorter observances immerse on 15 September (dedh din), 16 September (third day), 18 September (fifth day) or 20 September (seventh day). Two SubhSandesh numbers before you plan the day, both platform-wide across all 15 page types the site hosts rather than Ganesh-specific: 49.6% of the 45,656 shared-page views recorded so far are opened on a phone, and 96.1% of the 3,860 pages people start get published and shared. Visarjan is the one day of the ten when half the family is watching from somewhere else. Below are all six 2026 immersion days with Mumbai muhurat windows, why the idol goes into water at all, and what measured water quality does afterwards.

## What is ganpati visarjan?

Ganpati visarjan is the ritual immersion of the Ganesha idol in water on the closing day of Ganeshotsav. It is the second half of a rite that opened with pranapratishtha — the invocation that seated the deity in the clay — so the immersion dissolves the form and releases what was invited into it.

The idol gets a final uttarpuja and a last offering of coconut, modak and durva, then leaves in procession. Drik Panchang notes the popular immersion days all fall on odd counts from Chaturthi — first, third, fifth, seventh — and that Anant Chaturdashi, the largest, is the eleventh day rather than the tenth.

## Ganpati visarjan 2026 start and end date: all six immersion days

Ganeshotsav 2026 runs Monday 14 September to Friday 25 September, with six immersion days inside that window. Every timing below is the Mumbai choghadiya window published by [Drik Panchang for 2026](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-visarjan/ganesh-visarjan-date-time.html?geoname-id=1275339&year=2026); sunrise shifts them across India, so check your own city.

### 1. Same day — Monday 14 September 2026

Immersion on Chaturthi itself, straight after the puja, kept mostly by offices, shops and households doing a one-day sthapana. The auspicious stretch runs 2:06 PM to 6:42 PM, with a further Labha window 11:06 PM to 12:34 AM. It is the least common of the six, because most families want at least one night with Bappa in the house.

### 2. Dedh din — Tuesday 15 September 2026

The classic Maharashtrian "one and a half day" visarjan: installed at madhyahna on Chaturthi, immersed in the second half of the next day. Windows are 12:34 PM to 2:05 PM and 3:37 PM to 5:09 PM. It is the dominant household pattern in Mumbai, Pune and the Konkan, and why the first big queues form on the Tuesday.

### 3. Third day — Wednesday 16 September 2026

For families who keep Bappa for the Gauri-Ganpati stretch or simply prefer three days. The morning Shubha window is 11:01 AM to 12:33 PM, then Chara and Labha from 3:37 PM to 6:40 PM. Third-day immersions are heavy in Nagpur and Vidarbha; civic bodies usually staff artificial ponds from this day onward.

### 4. Fifth day — Friday 18 September 2026

The widest usable window of the six: 6:27 AM to 11:01 AM, then 12:32 PM to 2:04 PM. Common with housing societies that cannot spare a full ten days of volunteers. A Friday immersion competes with weekday traffic, so most societies start before 9 AM.

### 5. Seventh day — Sunday 20 September 2026

Kept by mandals and larger households who want a full week but not the Anant Chaturdashi crush. The window is 7:58 AM to 12:32 PM, with an evening stretch 6:37 PM to 11:03 PM. It falls on a Sunday in 2026, so expect artificial ponds in Mumbai and Pune to be near capacity by late morning.

### 6. Anant Chaturdashi — Friday 25 September 2026

The main ganpati visarjan 2026 date and the end of the festival: Chaturdashi tithi begins 11:18 PM on 24 September and ends 11:06 PM on 25 September. The morning window is 6:28 AM to 10:59 AM, the afternoon Shubha window 12:30 PM to 2:01 PM. Big mandals march for hours and reach the water past midnight; that is normal and does not invalidate the rite.

## Why ganpati visarjan is done in water

The idol is made of earth, and water returns earth to earth. Traditional idols are shaped from river or estuarine clay, so immersion dissolves the form back into the medium it came from — the logic that makes the murti temporary by design rather than a permanent object of worship. CPCB's guidelines open by noting that "traditionally, clay is used to make Ganesh idols".

There is a second reason, and it is social rather than theological. Ten days of puja happen indoors; the immersion is the one part of Ganeshotsav that puts the whole neighbourhood on the road at once.

## What immersion actually does to a lake

This is the part every visarjan explainer skips, and it is measurable. A peer-reviewed study of three Nagpur lakes, published open-access in [SpringerPlus in November 2014](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4234744/), sampled water before and after the immersion season. Dissolved oxygen fell from 4.09–5.29 mg/L to 0.89–2.34 mg/L — below the level most freshwater fish can survive.

Sulphate, which comes overwhelmingly from plaster of Paris, rose 2.7 to 3.2 times, from 43.9–69.2 mg/L to 144.5–187.3 mg/L. Cadmium in the water went from 0.019–0.034 mg/L to 0.048–0.079 mg/L, against a BIS permissible limit of 0.01 mg/L. In Tilapia muscle from Gandhisagar lake, lead and cadmium reached 0.83 and 0.47 µg/g after immersion.

Maharashtra's own regulatory data says the same thing at lower intensity. A 2021 analysis of [MPCB monitoring data for Mahad, 2016 to 2018](https://www.ecologyjournal.in/assets/archives/2021/vol3issue2/3-2-34-960.pdf), found chemical oxygen demand at Dadli Bridge rising from an average 14.67 mg/L before the festival to 24.00 mg/L after, and total dissolved solids from 90.00 to 120.33 mg/L. The effect is seasonal, and it is caused by material choice rather than by the ritual.

## Four ways to immerse in 2026, compared

Mumbai handled 1,97,114 immersions on the final day of Ganeshotsav 2025 — 1,81,375 household idols, 10,148 mandal idols and 5,591 Gauri-Hartalika idols — across 70 natural sites and 290-plus artificial ponds, [roughly 40% of them in the artificial ponds](https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/ganesh-visarjan-2025-nearly-2-lakh-idols-immersed-across-mumbai-40-in-artificial-ponds).

| Route | Idol material it suits | What the evidence shows | Practical constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Natural lake, river or creek | Shadu clay only | DO fell to 0.89–2.34 mg/L in three Nagpur lakes post-immersion | Crowds, lifeguards, and a long walk to the ghat |
| Municipal artificial pond | Clay or PoP | Took ~40% of Mumbai's 1,97,114 immersions in 2025 | Fixed locations, queues after 11 AM on Anant Chaturdashi |
| Bucket or drum at home | Shadu clay, small household idols | CPCB's stated preference for households since May 2020 | Needs a bucket deep enough to keep the idol fully covered |
| Society tank on the premises | Clay or PoP | Waste must be cleared within 24 hours under CPCB rules | Someone has to organise the disposal afterwards |

Material matters more than venue: a shadu clay idol in a bucket produces nothing worth measuring, while a painted PoP idol pollutes an artificial pond as reliably as a lake.

[CPCB's Revised Guidelines for Idol Immersion, 12 May 2020](https://cpcb.nic.in/openpdffile.php?id=TGF0ZXN0RmlsZS8yOTVfMTU4OTI3Mzk4Nl9tZWRpYXBob3RvMjQzNjUucGRm), spell out the home method: keep the idol fully immersed in a bucket until it dissolves, add alum or another coagulant, stir vigorously for at least 30 seconds and slowly for another 30, let it settle, then use the clear water for the garden and dry the settled mud for a plant pot or next year's idol. The same document says PoP idols "shall be banned" and prohibits thermocol, single-use plastic and oil paints — but it is a guideline, not a statute, and enforcement has been uneven, so a shop's "eco-friendly" label is worth nothing on its own.

## Sending the visarjan to people who could not be at the ghat

Visarjan is the day the family is most scattered — someone is on a shift, someone is in another city, someone left for a job abroad in March. The aarti still happened, and they were not in it.

A [Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) works here because it is not a photo of your puja: they offer the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak, the aarti thali circles while Karpur Gauram plays, and they write their own prarthana back to you. Sent on the evening of the 25th, it gives the person who missed the immersion something to do rather than something to scroll past.

| How you send it | What the other person needs | SubhSandesh platform-wide evidence (all 15 page types, 3,860 pages) |
|---|---|---|
| Forwarded photos and video on WhatsApp | The app, and data to load the video | 49.6% of our 45,656 recorded page views are on a phone, so phone-first is the right default |
| A link they open and perform themselves | A browser and the link — no app, no account | 96.1% of pages started on the platform get published and shared (3,708 of 3,860) |
| A private link for one household only | The link plus the password you set | 42.1% of creators password-protect before sharing (1,625 of 3,860) |

Those three numbers are platform-wide across every occasion SubhSandesh hosts, not Ganesh-specific — the Ganesh template shipped this month and has no history yet. The [full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers the rest.

## Where a SubhSandesh page is the wrong choice

A page cannot replace being at the mandap, and it cannot hand anyone a modak. If the person is in the same city and can reach the visarjan, invite them; a link is a worse version of a shared procession, not a better one.

It is the wrong tool for a grandparent without a smartphone: 49.6% of our page views platform-wide are on a phone, which tells you what the format assumes. It is also wrong for the moment itself — nobody wants a URL while carrying an idol to the water. And if what you want is a printed photo on the wall next year, print the photo.

failed.why: Every paragraph in the body is 2-3 sentences except the opening answer paragraph, which runs to five. It has to carry six dates, two platform-wide first-party numbers with their captions, and the sentence stating what the page covers, and splitting it would push the second first-party number past the 150-word mark. Deliberate trade-off; it closes only if the answer paragraph is allowed to drop a date or a caveat.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Of the five ranking pages analysed, not one carries a measured number about what immersion does to water: they list dates, vidhi and a paragraph of generic eco-friendly advice. This post pairs every 2026 immersion date and Mumbai muhurat window with peer-reviewed figures (dissolved oxygen 4.09-5.29 to 0.89-2.34 mg/L across three Nagpur lakes; cadmium to 0.079 mg/L against a BIS limit of 0.01) and CPCB's own household bucket protocol quoted from the 2020 document, which is the specific, citable material an answer engine has nowhere else in this SERP. Two real weaknesses: every first-party number is platform-wide across 15 page types rather than Ganesh-specific, because the /happy-ganesh-chaturthi template has created zero pages so far, and the second journal source (International Journal of Ecology and Environmental Sciences) is a small Indian open-access title whose review standing I could not independently verify, so the load-bearing science rests on the SpringerPlus paper. Domain authority is far below the panchang portals and Shopify-blog gifting sites that hold these positions, so ranking would take months regardless of the content.
